slice.child: compare probabilistic locally minted nonce plus predecessor binding against deterministic repository-derived creation identity for restore/clone ABA rejection
slice.candidate: Store each logical incarnation as {nonce, predecessor_binding, payload}; require stale writers to present the current incarnation token before mutation. Prefer an independently generated CSPRNG nonce rather than a deterministic path/blob/creation identity.

comparison.deterministic_repository_identity: Path and identical content/blob can repeat; deterministic identity therefore does not establish a new incarnation.
comparison.fresh_nonce_plus_predecessor: If recreation mints a new independent nonce, stale equality admission fails except on nonce collision; predecessor binding also exposes accidental chain splicing.

comparison.case: exact copy or clone of the whole state
comparison.fresh_nonce_plus_predecessor: Also replays the stored nonce and predecessor chain exactly; no freshness gain against a whole-state copy/clone.

comparison.case: rollback or historical resurrection of the whole state
comparison.deterministic_repository_identity: Old identity becomes current again, recreating ABA.
comparison.fresh_nonce_plus_predecessor: Old nonce and predecessor prefix become current again too. A stale writer from that historical incarnation can match. Predecessor binding does not help when the entire prefix is resurrected.

comparison.case: recreate old payload but force a newly minted nonce
comparison.fresh_nonce_plus_predecessor: Rejects stale incarnation probabilistically; this is the narrow scope where the nonce is materially stronger.

collision_analysis.scope_note: These are ideal-uniform bounds. They do not cover RNG state replay, model-generated token entropy, nonce forgery, or copying/restoring the nonce itself.

slice.inference: Randomness solves accidental identity reuse only when every logical recreation actually obtains fresh entropy that is not rolled back with the repository. It cannot, by itself, provide a non-replayable incarnation source when the adversarial/failure model permits exact repository clone or rollback. The predecessor link detects partial splices but a full historical-prefix replay preserves it. Therefore nonce+predecessor is not a general substitute for a monotone/non-replayable freshness authority.
slice.decision: Do not elevate nonce+predecessor to a general Phase-1 freshness primitive. Retain it as a low-cost probabilistic hardening layer under an explicit non-replay assumption; continue searching for a Chat-native non-replayable freshness source or a repository operation with an expected-old-state precondition that survives ordinary rollback/recreation.

public_sources.claims: UUIDv4 carries 122 random bits; Section 6.8 notes true global uniqueness cannot be guaranteed without shared knowledge; Section 6.9 recommends a CSPRNG and reseeding across state changes such as forks.

Git object names are content-derived and identical content stored in different repositories has the same object name, so object identity is deliberately clone/copy-stable rather than an incarnation token.

tested_scope: Analytic/synthetic single logical pointer with equality admission; one stale writer; deterministic repository path/blob/creation-style identity versus an ideal independent 122-bit UUIDv4-like or raw 128-bit nonce plus predecessor binding; fresh delete/recreate, exact whole-state copy/clone, whole-state rollback/historical resurrection, and collision assumptions. No live repository mutation, branch-ref CAS, multi-object atomicity, network partition, protected coordination, server audit-log uniqueness, adversarial nonce forgery, RNG implementation audit, or cryptographic collision experiment was tested.

phase1_constraints.reason: General restore/clone freshness remains unresolved; the random-nonce benefit is conditional on a fresh entropy source whose state is not replayed with the repository.
